memory_candidates: In Cslib/Logics/Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic/Scheme.lean, intUniverse/intExpMeasure/intSubfmls/intWork are declared AFTER intExpandBranches_openBranch_sat and after tableau_complete. Any future work needing to reference intUniverse/intExpMeasure in intExpandBranches_openBranch_sat's own signature will hit a forward-reference build error and must relocate that block first. A prior (superseded) v6-plan handoff independently hit and noted this same constraint when placing new lemmas 'after intExpMeasure_init_le_fuel... since Lean requires forward declaration.'

Lean's `induction ... generalizing x y z` automatically reverts (and forces case-by-case re-proof of) any hypothesis in context that depends on x/y/z, even if not named in the generalizing list. This means a plan that splits 'add new invariant hypotheses to a recursive lemma's signature' (one phase) from 'maintain them across the recursive cases' (a later phase) is not actually separable once those hypotheses are added -- the moment they exist and mention a generalized variable, every existing recursive call site must supply them.

intExpandBranches_world_bound (nextWorld <= phi0.complexity + 1, needed to bound freshly-created tableau worlds within the fixed finite intUniverse) is explicitly documented in Cslib/Logics/Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic/Scheme.lean (three places: ~2025-2038, ~2052-2055, ~2536-2538) as an unbuilt 'continuation, see handoff' -- it requires a new injection argument (worlds created -> distinct .imp-node positions of phi0's parse tree, using the already-proven intSubfmls_impCount_le as the combinatorial ingredient) and should be budgeted as its own phase, not assumed available inside adjacent invariant-threading work.

For the intuitionistic tableau's base-3 damped worklist measure (intExpMeasure = sum of 3^intWork per branch), every summand is >= 1 unconditionally (3^n >= 1 for all n:Nat). This means 'measure <= fuel' with fuel=0 forces the branches list to be EMPTY, not merely 'fully saturated' -- the fuel=0 base case of a measure-driven termination argument closes by a short contradiction (nonempty branches -> measure >= 1 > 0) whenever the caller's postcondition (e.g. .openBranch b) itself requires a nonempty branches list, rather than needing the more elaborate 'measure=0 implies every cell already recorded' argument one might first reach for.
